abstract:
Abstract
                  Artificial intelligence (AI) is reshaping marketing as firms increasingly delegate activities and decisions previously performed by marketers to AI systems. As AI assumes a greater role in market-facing decisions, understanding the value firms realize from these investments becomes increasingly important. Building on marketing accountability and resource-based theory, we develop a Return on AI (RoAI) framework that conceptualizes AI investment through the people, processes, and capabilities that enable its deployment and governance. RoAI evaluates incremental benefit while accounting for value retention, evidence durability, and the full costs of deployment over time. The framework identifies a distinctive consequence of delegated judgment, wherein AI can improve current performance while reducing the experiential practice through which marketers develop and maintain the judgment required to evaluate and redirect the AI solution. This mechanism helps explain heterogeneity in AI returns across firms and over time. We develop seven testable predictions and an agenda for research on creating, appropriating, and sustaining value from AI.

ob.ai_reason: 营销组织AI投资回报框架，AI+营销核心
ob.tldr: 基于营销问责制与资源基础观，构建评估营销组织AI投资回报的RoAI框架，从人员、流程与能力三维度衡量AI部署与治理的增量收益、价值留存、证据持久性与全周期成本。揭示"委托判断"机制——AI虽能提升当前绩效，却削弱营销人员通过实践积累评估与纠偏AI的判断能力，从而解释企业间与时间维度上AI回报的异质性，并提出七项可检验预测与未来研究议程。

title: Return on AI (RoAI): A framework for assessing AI investments in the marketing organization
